title: The Secret of the Acorn King
moral: The treasure grows when shared with kindness.

story:
On the first warm Saturday of spring, three boys met at the edge of Maplewood Park. Theo was careful and kind, Max was energetic and playful, and Jay was thoughtful and observant. While exploring near an old picnic shelter, they found a strange engraved stone hidden under ivy. It had swirling carvings and a crowned acorn symbol. Nearby, they discovered a message scratched into the wood: LOOK FOR THE ACORN KING. THE TREASURE IS SEALED BEHIND THE ENGRAVED STONE. SHARE WHAT YOU FIND.

Excited, the boys tried to open the stone but could not move it. Jay noticed a clue on a park map pointing to a place called the Acorn Oak. They decided to follow the trail. At the base of a large oak tree, they found a wooden box. Inside was a map and a small brass key. The map said: THE STONE OPENS WHEN THE PARK HEARS KINDNESS. BRING THREE SIGNS: WATER, LIGHT, AND LAUGHTER. THEN USE THE KEY. AND REMEMBER—SHARE.

Understanding the message, the boys decided to act kindly. On their way back, they cleaned up scattered trash in the park together. Then they returned to the stone and followed the steps. Theo gently sprinkled water around the stone. Jay reflected sunlight using a shiny wrapper. Max made everyone laugh with his jokes. Then Theo found a small notch and used the key. With a soft click, the stone slid open.

Inside, they found a tin box filled with small treasures: glass marbles, wooden animals, star stickers, blank cards, and chocolate coins. A note inside read: THIS TREASURE GROWS WHEN SHARED.

The boys smiled. Instead of taking everything, they chose a few small items each. Then they wrote kind messages on the blank cards for future explorers. They placed most of the treasure back into the tin, along with their notes.

Finally, they returned the box, placed the key back inside, and carefully closed the stone. As they walked home, they realized the greatest treasure was not what they found, but what they shared—kindness, teamwork, and joy.

Deep in Maplewood Park, beneath the ivy, the stone rested quietly once more, waiting for the next kind and curious explorers.
